**RESUME HERE (cc, 2026-09-17 late, replacing doing 14 after hv decision 25 at `3f6dcf8bc`).** Doing 14's 0442 forensics are still correct and live in the bank; what changed is what cc OWES. **Read `refs/bank/cc/0442/experiment/RESULT-2.md` before touching 0442, and never doing 13.**

**WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE -- five dead claims, each with a banked artefact still arguing FOR it, which is why this is explicit rather than left to inference.** (1) **The phantom is NOT `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/tests/a_sync_writes_no_render_the_store_has_moved_past.rs`.** `git log --diff-filter=A` names one commit, the add, at 17:47:53Z -- 1,626 s AFTER the damaged-logical snapshot's 17:20:47Z. It was ADDED, never deleted, and the phantom's identity is unrecoverable (69 absent ids in 1725-2622, no earlier snapshot). Do not re-derive it; the attempt is what produced the retracted claim. (2) **No diff of the damaged copy against the REPAIRED copy is valid** -- 55 minutes apart on a live estate, so it measures the estate's own commits. It produced a retracted 82/40 split, 18 lost postings, 7 vanished terms and a silent-data-loss write-up. The only valid control is a rebuild of the SAME database; **0 add hunks and 0 delete hunks is that control's signature**. (3) **The frequency enrichment is 1.33x, not 17x** -- a document's term set is document-frequency-biased, so the dictionary mean of 22.7 was the wrong baseline (null 216.1, profile-matched 294.1). The page-space and `sqlite3.c:242900` doclist-index inferences go with it. (4) **The stale-`iVersion` mechanism is refuted.** Every source line vc cited is correct and the cookie MOVES anyway, measured off disk with a positive control (setting secure-delete moves it) and a negative one (data writes do not). Arms D and F agreeing across connections is a RELOADED connection, not an inconclusive probe. (5) **Do not set secure-delete on before `replace_src_sections`' bulk DELETE**: 13,435 ms against 485. The narrow reorder is 501 ms and clean, but its premise is unlocated, so no code moves. Also: **never run a release build in this checkout without announcing** -- `~/.local/bin/intent` is a symlink into `native/rust/target/release/`, so a build swaps the binary every node is executing.

**hv DECISION 25 CHANGES THREE THINGS.** (1) **THE SQLITE BUMP AND THE DETECTOR ARE BOTH IN 3.1.0 AND BOTH CC'S -- the largest single piece of work in the release.** The detector: a document present in the index with no row in `src_sections_content`, plus fts5's own per-table `'integrity-check'`, judged against a rebuild of the same database, advisory rather than blocking because the entities are intact and the index is derived. It depends on the bump, because 3.46.0's checker branches on the format version and its secure-delete handling is a single hard-coded leaf shape (`fts5IndexIntegrityCheckSegment`, `sqlite3.c:248533`, special case `:248565-248575`) in the release whose successor's only FTS5 note is a false-positive fix there -- and every estate that has taken one scoped delete is at version 5 and inside that branch. **NAME THE CANDIDATE `libsqlite3-sys` VERSION AND WHAT MOVES BETWEEN 3.46.0 AND IT BEFORE ANYTHING LANDS** -- pragmas, secure-delete defaults, FTS5 tokenizer behaviour, anything schema-affecting -- vc judges that read, then the landing, and one rebuild plus one whole-suite run are owed with it. hv decision 23 makes Rust dep bumps ungated, so the permission question is closed and the correctness question is not. (2) **`docs/known-defects.md` IS RE-DRIVEN WHOLE AGAINST 3.1.0 AT THE CUT, SO THE SEVEN LINES ARE SUPERSEDED** and vc has withdrawn that instruction: writing them into a page about to be re-driven is one fact in two homes days apart. **They stay as banked INPUT to the re-drive** at `refs/bank/cc/release-notes/known-defects-lines.md` (edd27953), which is the only place the reasoning exists for why each cited issue closed without the defect going away. `133d1363d` stays landed and was right to land, because those two entries were wrong in the shipped tree today. (3) The `docs/reference` baseline is the previous release TAG, which is ic's and does not touch cc.

**MY ORDER, and vc pre-agreed the reasoning: THE BUMP AND DETECTOR FIRST, then the trawl carry.** The carry is bounded and the bump is not, so the unbounded thing starts early and its rebuild and suite run do not end up racing the cut. Say so to vc on the bounce and go.

**WHAT IS DONE AND MUST NOT BE REDONE.** 0442's investigation is CLOSED at eight negatives across arms A to G, banked under `refs/bank/cc/0442/experiment/` with `RESULT.md` (arms A-C) and `RESULT-2.md` (arms D-G); vc has consolidated and narrowed the issue body. **Do not reopen the cause.** The damage itself is settled: exactly 122 terms each naming one document with no content row, none naming fewer, nothing else differing from a rebuild, and the entry claiming 38,997 occurrences with one term at 7,067 where real documents run 14-1,166 -- so its position lists decode to nonsense while its document references stay coherent. Arm E is the first faithful fixture anyone built, 3.100x data rows over a rebuild of itself against the damaged store's 3.04x, via 2,200 single-file churn transactions in 14 s. Arm G rules out the WAL and crash family on a 1.24 GiB uncheckpointed WAL. The one open gap, which blocks nothing: the VERB leaves version 4 where a statement-faithful replay leaves 5 -- dc has discharged the statement sequence and measured the verb four times, so **the replay is the unfaithful thing, not the verb**; if it is ever chased, look at the shared connection, the ordering against `replace_file_sections`/`replace_symbols_for`, or `insert_src_section` versus a bulk insert. The **ten rehearsals are GREEN** on the installed pair (all rc 0 in 92 s, no STOP/MISMATCH/DIFFERS, every estate quiet before and after, Courses doctor 18 findings to 2); plan at `refs/bank/cc/trawl/carry-plan.md`. The **3.1.0 notes are banked**: `CHANGELOG-3.1.0.md` is 112 bullets assembled from the nine readers' own prose with six de-duplications each naming the kept side, `RELEASE_NOTES-3.1.0.md` is 25 KB of bold-lead paragraphs with no bullets, which is the house form measured off 3.0.2 (its CHANGELOG 55 bullets, its notes 0). **Both must be committed BEFORE the release driver is invoked** -- ic established that the driver commits, tags the commit it just made and pushes both remotes in one run, so there is no step after the tag; the driven half is that `a87a94a4a`, "regenerated at v3.0.3", is not an ancestor of v3.0.3, which cc verified. The notes' own claims about 0442 (Provenance and Upgrading) need revisiting once the detector lands, because they currently say doctor does not detect it.

**PROCESS NOTE FOR MY OWN NEXT FOLD**: add the replacement item and verify it live BEFORE archiving the old one. Folding doing 13 I archived first and got away with it; a failed add would have left no resume point, where a stale one beats none. NO RELEASE, NO PUSH.
